Definition: from a derivative of G2873; to feel fatigue; by implication, to work hard:--(bestow) labour, toil, be wearied.
KeyPassages: Matthew 6:28; Luke 5:5; John 4:6; Acts 20:35; Romans 16:6; 1 Corinthians 4:12
BiblicalUsage: Kopiao means to labour, to toil until weary. Matthew 6:28 says the lilies toil not, neither do they spin, Luke 5:5 has Simon saying, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing, John 4:6 has Jesus being wearied with His journey and sitting on Jacob's well, Acts 20:35 says so labouring ye ought to support the weak, Romans 16:6 greets Mary who bestowed much labour on us, and 1 Corinthians 4:12 has Paul labouring, working with his own hands.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the toil in these verses is the whole working life of the church: Simon toiling all night for nothing, Paul toiling with his hands, and Mary bestowing much labour. I hold that Jesus wearied with His journey is the centre of it, because the Lord of the harvest grew tired on the road to the well, and still stopped to save a woman.
RelatedBooks: Matthew; Luke; John; Acts; Romans; 1 Corinthians
